title: Give the availability window an OPENING gate, not only a closing one
objective: OfferFacts.available_from is carried from the column into the engine and then consulted by nothing, so an offer that has not opened yet can reach Z0_TRUE_FREE and publish 'Usage remains $0' about an offer that does not exist yet. Add the missing opening gate, and route an incoherent window to UNKNOWN.

grounds: Sibling-field precedent: available_until routes through _availability_reasons into the conditional list at engine.py:263. docs/DATA_MODEL.md gate 4 already reads 'bounded or expired availability windows'; a window bounded BELOW is a bounded window.
UNKNOWN in this engine is reserved for facts that could not be ESTABLISHED -- all four Gate-4 triggers are absence-of-knowledge. A dated future start is an established, evidenced fact.

Given identical safety (both are non-Z0), choose the class that EXPLAINS better. Z2 can say 'does not become available until 2030-01-01'. UNKNOWN would say 'cannot determine', which is LESS honest because we can determine it exactly.
design_decision.rejection_reasoning: The argument for it -- a bounded-but-open offer is verifiable NOW, a not-yet-open one is not -- is real, but it is a statement about EVIDENCE QUALITY, not about the material condition. This product already models evidence currency on a separate axis (coverage snapshots, the evidence floor, last_verified_at, the adviser stale-evidence path). Folding 'known but not yet observable' into the class taxonomy would hide an evidence concern from the machinery built to handle it, and overload UNKNOWN with a second meaning. 'Unknown is better than guessed' is a rule against GUESSING; we hold a date.

second_decision_approved_by_owner.why: The engine module docstring and the DATA_MODEL.md safety invariant already promise that an unknown OR CONTRADICTORY material condition yields UNKNOWN. Leaving it would be a knowing gap against documented behaviour and would publish two mutually contradictory sentences about one offer.
second_decision_approved_by_owner.precedence_consequence: It CANNOT live in _availability_reasons, which feeds the conditional list at Gate 5. UNKNOWN is decided at Gate 4, which PRECEDES Gate 5. It therefore needs a separate helper feeding the Gate-4 unknown list.
second_decision_approved_by_owner.clock_independence: The helper takes no as_of. A contradiction between two stored dates is a contradiction regardless of the clock, so this adds NO new as_of-dependence and cannot complicate the PR #100 invariant.
second_decision_approved_by_owner.cannot_touch_the_permit_arm: It fires only when BOTH dates are non-null and inverted, so an offer with available_from alone never reaches it.

the_asymmetry_that_must_not_be_tidied_aw: available_until emits a reason on BOTH sides of its boundary. available_from must emit a reason on ONE side only (future). A start date already reached imposes no ongoing bound. If a future refactor 'symmetrises' the two, EVERY offer with a past start date becomes Z2 and the product wrongly WITHHOLDS genuinely free offers at scale -- the failure this project weights equally with wrongly asserting one. Boundary is strictly '>': available_from == as_of means the offer opens today, so it is available and emits no reason.

pr_100_invariant_handling.prediction_contradicting_the_brief: The brief expected this test to break. I predict it PASSES UNCHANGED: its facts come from _facts(), which leaves available_from=None, and the new gate is `is not None`-guarded so it cannot fire. The EXECUTED invariant was always a statement about available_until alone.

Docstring re-scoped to state what it always actually measured.
Scope pinned executably by passing available_from=None explicitly, so a future change to _facts() defaults cannot drift the test out of the population its claim covers. This is a TIGHTENING edit.
Mutation M4 proves it still kills its ORIGINAL target after the re-scope. A re-scoped guard that no longer catches its original defect IS a weakened guard.
The new property is added as a SEPARATE test, never by editing this one.
pr_100_invariant_handling.stop_condition: If treatment items 1-4 cannot all be achieved, STOP AND REPORT rather than ship a blunted guard.

verification_method.baseline_rule: A baseline must be shown to have EXECUTED at least one test, not merely to have exited 0. Assert collected N > 0; pytest exit 5 means NOTHING COLLECTED.
verification_method.mutation_rule: Every mutation must RESTORE THE ORIGINAL DEFECT while keeping the code valid -- not merely break the call. An arity break kills on TypeError and proves nothing about behaviour. Pre-grep the search text before each run and ABORT if absent: an unapplied mutation reads exactly like a surviving one.
verification_method.environment_rule: Preconditions asserted, not announced. .venv is ABSENT in this worktree (bootstrap incomplete, documented). Global interpreter is Python 3.13.15 with pytest 9.0.3, matching the pyproject pin. For the DB arm, verify the database is present in pg_database and a trivial query succeeds BEFORE any verdict, and compare runtime against baseline -- a large deviation is evidence about the environment, not the code. A false KILL confirms whatever you hoped.
verification_method.no_static_type_checker: requirements-dev carries ruff, pytest, detect-secrets, pip-audit, httpx, cryptography. No mypy, no pyright. Keyword-only requirements are enforced at RUNTIME as TypeError; no static gate will be claimed.
verification_method.powershell_trap: Select-Object -First/-Last corrupts $LASTEXITCODE. Exit codes read from BARE calls only.
verification_method.timezone: No TZ-sensitive probe on this host: Windows CPython has no time.tzset() and silently ignores TZ. The new gate is date-comparison only and needs none.
verification_method.database: Own postgres:16-alpine on unused port 55433 with a named volume, seeded separately from the suite's DB, alembic upgrade head applied. REMOVED at end of session -- container AND volume -- with the exact removal commands and output reported.
